items.title: Bill Watrous interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 26, 1999
items.q: he was attached to the Archbishop in Salzburg’s court

ctx.x: Oh it’s incredible. The stuff that’s in here, you realize you know when you read all of the other accounts of Mozart’s life, he wasn’t all in that poverty area, he was treated like a © Fillius Jazz Archive -20-

nobleman when he traveled all over Europe, I mean years of course he was attached to the Archbishop in Salzburg’s court, but he was given leave with his father to travel all over to all of the cities of Europe and made really copious sums of money for his tremendous feats of music. I mean the guy was writing masses and symphonies at the age of nine, and composing at the age of four and five, I mean it was just phenomenal what we know about this man.
